explanation_text:
This is a network traffic summary for a network with four devices (of:0000000000000001, of:0000000000000002, of:0000000000000003, and of:0000000000000004) connected through two links (s1-s2 and s2-s3). The summary includes data for four different time periods: pre-injection, post-injection at 10 seconds, post-injection at 30 seconds, post-injection at 50 seconds, and recovery.

During the pre-injection period, there were no flows recorded. After injection at 10 seconds, there were a total of 83 flows, with devices of:0000000000000001, of:0000000000000002, of:0000000000000003, and of:0000000000000004 all available. The links s1-s2 and s2-s3 were active, and the host IPs were 10.1.0.1, 10.1.0.2, 10.1.0.3, 10.1.0.5, and 10.1.0.6.

At 30 seconds and 50 seconds post-injection, the number of flows decreased to 73 and then remained constant at 29. The devices and links remained the same, but the host IPs changed slightly.

During the recovery period, all devices were available, and the links and host IPs remained the same as in the post-injection periods. The total number of flows increased to 30.

The Open vSwitch (OVS) flow summary shows the number of total rules and drop rules on each switch (s1, s2, s3, and s4) at different time periods. The number of rules and drop rules increased significantly after injection and then decreased over time.

The connectivity section includes ping and iperf data. The ping data shows the loss percentage and round-trip time (RTT) between hosts h1 and h2 and devices 10.1.0.3 and 10.1.0.4. After injection, the connectivity between h1 and 10.1.0.4 was lost, while the connectivity between h2 and 10.1.0.3 remained. The iperf data shows the throughput, lost percentage, and retransmits for a network test, but no such data was recorded during the time periods in question.
